title: Tor bounds descend from bounded flat local models
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\Gamma$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $\Gamma_T=p_T^*\Gamma$ for schemes $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $Q\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Gamma_S))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $\{g_i:V_i\to S\}_{i=1}^n$ is a finite covering family of $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-site]. Fix integers $r\le s$ and cochain complexes $L_i^\bullet$ of $\Gamma_{V_i}$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], with $L_i^q=0$ for $q\notin[r,s]$, all terms flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and isomorphisms $g_i^*Q\simeq L_i^\bullet$ in the derived category. Then for every $\Gamma_S$-module $N$ placed in degree zero,
$$g_i^*(Q\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Gamma_S}N)\simeq L_i^\bullet\otimes_{\Gamma_{V_i}}g_i^*N.$$
Here $g_i^*$ is the exact inverse-image functor with the pulled-back coefficient ring. The tensor on the right is ordinary tensor of complexes. Moreover $H^q(Q\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Gamma_S}N)=0$ for every $q\notin[r,s]$ and every $N$. Equivalently, $Q$ has Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$ [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude].

source.place: (2) Local models, global bounds: K-flat local tensor calculation and checking vanishing on a cover

proof.text: For each $i$, identify $(V_i)_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with $S_{\mathrm{proét}}/V_i$ by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1). Under this site identification inverse image is restriction, with the section formula of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The ring isomorphism $g_i^{-1}\Gamma_S\cong\Gamma_{V_i}$ of [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] identifies module inverse image with restriction and transport of the ring action. Thus, for a module sheaf $F$, $(g_i^*F)(W\to V_i)=F(W\to S)$ after this coefficient identification. Here only clause (1) of the localization lemma is used; its constant-ring clauses are not applied to the condensed ring $\Gamma$.

source.place: Tag 098K (definition-big-small-proetale); sites.tex Tags 00XZ (section-localize), 00Y0 (definition-localize), and sites-modules.tex Tag 04IX (definition-localize-ringed-site)

proof.text: The functor $g_i^*$ is exact, as stipulated in the statement. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], $H^q(g_i^*A^\bullet)\cong g_i^*H^q(A^\bullet)$ for every complex. In particular it preserves every quasi-isomorphism. Hence its termwise action induces $D(g_i^*)$ on the derived category. To identify this with $Lg_i^*$, choose for a representative $A^\bullet$ a K-flat flat-term resolution $P^\bullet\to A^\bullet$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The computation in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] identifies $Lg_i^*A$ with the image of $g_i^*P^\bullet$, and exactness makes $g_i^*P^\bullet\to g_i^*A^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism. These comparison maps give $Lg_i^*A\cong D(g_i^*)A$. Write both as $g_i^*A$ below.

Fix any $\Gamma_S$-module $N$ in degree zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the ringed-topos morphism $g_i$ and the two objects $Q,N[0]$. Step 2 turns its derived pullbacks into exact inverse images and gives
$$g_i^*(Q\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Gamma_S}N)\cong (g_i^*Q)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Gamma_{V_i}}(g_i^*N).$$
Use the given isomorphism $g_i^*Q\cong L_i^\bullet$ in this bifunctor to replace the first factor by $L_i^\bullet$. No flatness of $N$ is used.

Each $L_i^\bullet$ is bounded above by $s$ and has flat terms. Therefore it is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. To compute its tensor with $g_i^*N$ using precisely an existing ringed-site statement, specialize the representative-computation clause of [lem-trf-site-derived-tensor-restriction] to $\mathcal R=\mathcal S=\Gamma_{V_i}$, $\varphi=\mathrm{id}$, $H=Q_{\Gamma_{V_i}}(L_i^\bullet)$, and the K-flat flat-term representative $\mathrm{id}:L_i^\bullet\to L_i^\bullet$. That clause explicitly says that its left derived object is computed by $P\otimes_{\mathcal R}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi N$. For this identity ring map it is exactly $L_i^\bullet\otimes_{\Gamma_{V_i}}g_i^*N$. Together with step 3 this is the asserted local isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat) and Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor and its preceding construction)

proof.text: By the total-complex formula [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], tensoring $L_i^\bullet$ with the degree-zero complex $g_i^*N$ has degree-$q$ term $L_i^q\otimes_{\Gamma_{V_i}}g_i^*N$. This term is zero whenever $q\notin[r,s]$. Its degree-$q$ cohomology is then zero, since $\ker(0\to C^{q+1})/\operatorname{im}(C^{q-1}\to0)=0$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $F^q=H^q(Q\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Gamma_S}N)$. Applying the cohomology comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] and the local isomorphism of step 4 gives $g_i^*F^q=0$ for every $i$ and every $q\notin[r,s]$.

source.place: Tag 06YL (section-flat), total tensor used before Lemma 06YM (lemma-derived-tor-exact); homology.tex Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor)

proof.text: Fix $q\notin[r,s]$ and an arbitrary object $W\to S$ of the site. The covering axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1)(iii) gives the covering $\{W\times_SV_i\to W\}_i$. Step 1 and the restriction formula [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] give $F^q(W\times_SV_i)=0$, since $F^q|_{V_i}=0$. For any $x\in F^q(W)$, all its restrictions equal those of the zero section. The equalizer (in particular uniqueness) part of the sheaf condition in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) therefore gives $x=0$. Thus every section group of $F^q$ is zero, so $F^q=0$. The argument also works for an empty covering, by the empty equalizer sheaf condition. Since $N$ and $q\notin[r,s]$ were arbitrary, this is exactly Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$ by [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude](3).

split_report.summary: Kept the statement and coefficient category unchanged. Expanded the local calculation using exact inverse image, the general ringed-topos tensor comparison, bounded-above-flat K-flatness, and the identity-ring specialization of an existing representative-computation lemma. Proved vanishing descent by separatedness on each base-changed cover. Reused all auxiliary facts: no new nodes. Corrected the 06YS/06YQ bibliographic mismatch only in this split and report.
